BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents have been reviewed as counterparty material.

## Headline points

1. **No fallback authority exists.** The Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month claims period match our conditional fallbacks exactly. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for either, so we cannot accept them. We hold at 25% and 24 months.
2. **Fraud protection is removed without saying so.** The Seller does not mention fraud. Instead, clauses 9.3, 12.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply all limitations "to all Claims of any nature". In effect, fraud would be capped and time-barred. This is non-negotiable and no one can waive it.
3. **Two completion-critical items are unresolved.** The Disclosure Letter admits that there is no Bluefen consent (§2) and no Riverlark discharge (§3).
4. **The Seller's characterisations go further than its own disclosures.** For example, it calls tax and IP "settled", Bluefen "addressed", DD-006 "not expected to be material" and title "evidenced". The Disclosure Letter does not support any of these.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** Reason: 20% is a conditional fallback that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given. Escalate to her if movement is contemplated.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping.** Reason: the Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250k of valid claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. The Seller also wants any limitation to apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate periods for Fundamental and Title claims and for fraud.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** Reason: 18 months is an unauthorised fallback (no approval from Amelia Frost), and the default wording silently extends the general period to every category.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Reason: title is the asset we are buying, and capping it at 20% for six fewer years misprices the core risk.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright and insert an express overriding carve-out.** Reason: this is a red line that no one may waive, and the "any nature" wording would otherwise capture fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL §1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific and fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete DL §1.1–1.2 and the related Schedule 7 wording.** Reason: deemed disclosure of the whole data room and public registers shifts all diligence risk to us and undermines every warranty. Only the specific disclosures (§2–10) should stand, and only to the extent they are fair.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier should be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** Reason: "discoverable" plus "advisers" makes this effectively a total warranty bar, and it would neutralise the specific indemnities for matters we already know about, such as Ironquay.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). DL §2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions have been met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent under clause 11.2 **and** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective consent plus satisfied conditions a CP, with a stronger endeavours obligation.** Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m in FY26). A delivered but conditional consent may not be effective, and reasonable endeavours is too weak for a customer this material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion. DL §3 confirms the facility (about AUD 3.2m) has not been repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. The facility should be treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free price.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Reason: a post-completion release leaves encumbered shares and assets and change-of-control exposure under clause 8.1. The fallback (an irrevocable undertaking) also needs Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 in DD-005 bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or otherwise funded by the Seller, for example as a Debt-like deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion. Require an express line item, on-costs included.** Reason: the Company will be the paying employer after Completion, so unfunded bonuses become our cost. On-costs need to be confirmed and quantified, not assumed.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering IP ownership and infringement losses in the SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the clause 7.3 cure (payment of the SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Broaden the indemnity and add a CP or deliverable for payment evidence plus a confirmatory assignment.** Reason: under clause 7.3, title transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, so the risk is IP ownership, not just a fee. Note that the AUD 180k in DD-010 has not been independently verified as either paid or unpaid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation, regular updates before Completion, and appropriate warranty or indemnity protection. We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation and add investigation and update covenants.** Reason: DL §6 itself says access, scope and notification obligations are not established. The Seller cannot conclude the matter is immaterial, and we should not conclude it is a breach.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence to assess them. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and equally no automatic acceptance as ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the characterisation yet. Request the DD-008 and DD-011 terms** (termination rights, accruals, timing, whether the renewals are related-party or linked). Reason: DL §8 does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, so their classification cannot be settled either way.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime applies to all Claims. Limitations apply "unless expressly stated otherwise", and tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations (Debt, bonuses, funds flow) and covenants kept as separate categories, with no override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restructure clauses 12–13 by category and reverse the default** so that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Reason: the "any nature" and "unless stated" drafting is a hidden override that caps indemnities, covenants and payment obligations.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Examples include an ASIC extract, a PPSR search, share certificates, board and shareholder approvals, and a Riverlark release.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone and require independent evidence as CP or completion deliverables.** Reason: DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, which DL §10 effectively concedes, and the Riverlark security remains undischarged.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as **open**. They are not resolved, and we are not assuming unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" statement. Reserve tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Reason: no agreement has been reached, and accepting the general regime would import the 20% cap and 18-month limit by default.

---

## Escalation and next steps

- **Amelia Frost:** Inform her that the Seller has opened exactly at our fallbacks on the cap (20%) and the claims period (18 months). No authority currently exists for either. A Riverlark post-completion undertaking would also need her approval.
- **Information requests:** We should ask the Seller for:
  - the Bluefen clause 11.3 conditions and a consent pathway;
  - a Riverlark payout letter and release drafts;
  - a DD-005 on-cost calculation;
  - Ironquay payment evidence;
  - a DD-006 investigation status report and confirmation that logs are being preserved;
  - the Sandbar contract terms;
  - independent title searches.
- **Noted, not in scope:** The office lease (DD-007, notification only) and Mossvale (DD-009, assignment restriction) do not appear on their face to require consent to the share sale. We should confirm this when we review the full documents.
